text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Riga district court rejected a claim by the Latvian Social Democratic Party against Prime Minister Andris Shkele. The leader of the party, Juris Bojars, said he would appeal against the verdict.
- President Guntis Ulmanis continues his visit to Poland. Latvian entrepreneurs who accompanying Ulmanis had a meeting with Polish businessmen.
- Farmers will block several roads near Riga to stage a big protest action against the government's agricultural policy.
- Vents Balodis of Fatherland & Freedom replaced Robert Zile as chairman of the budget and finance committee.
- Latvia and Norway initialled an agreement on visa-free travel as well as on the re-admission of illegal immigrants.
- Riga deputy mayor Juris Ritins signed the declaration of Nantes on the organisation of environment-friendly transport in major European cities.

- The newspaper forecasts the possible distribution of Ventspils Nafta stock after privatisation. It says 35 percent of shares will be controlled by Latvian Oil Transit, a company which unites major Latvian businesses dealing in oil transit.
- The parliament committee for human rights accepted a bill on the status of refugees and asylum-seekers.
- The state board supervising the insurance business in Latvia cancelled the licence of insurance company Parex-dziviba after shareholders decided to liquidate the company.
- Unibanka signed an authorisation for Credit Suisse First Boston to co-ordinate the issue of its eurobonds.
- Cargos handled by Latvian ports over the first three months of 1997 rose 17.5 percent.
